message: SIMD ballot requires a two-word u32 result
internal: The device's simdgroup::ballot wrapper returns [u32; 2], so importing it always interns the two-word u32 array that ballot_type looks up.
Only simdgroup::shuffle* carry a source control, their control parameter is typed u32, and the importer passes the call's operands through unchanged.
simdgroup::any, all and ballot take predicate: bool and forward it unchanged to the vote intrinsic.

message: a check before a barrier or SIMD operation must be proved or uniform; a thread that fails it would leave the others waiting
a mutable reference requires a mutable path
internal: rustc's Derefer pass leaves at most one leading Deref in each MIR place and IR pointers keep their Rust mutability (types.rs with_spaces, checked by references.rs checked_reference), so every &mut or &raw mut that borrowck accepts goes through a mutable pointer or none (`&mut **p` through `&*mut u32` compiles).

message: a reference must point into one address space
a slice is not one value
internal: typed_place is only asked for sized MIR places (assignment and call destinations, discriminant reads, operands), and reference inference gives a local a slice pointer only when checked_reference confirms its Rust type points to a slice, so such a place never ends at a slice's elements.

message: a slice's data must be a thin pointer
internal: SliceFromParts comes only from RawPtr aggregates (core's from_raw_parts, whose data is `*const impl Thin` and lowers to a thin pointer; a zero-sized pointee lowers to Unit and fails reference inference with `unsupported reference type`) and from two-field #[repr(transparent)] wrappers, whose zero-sized second field fails the earlier usize length check (`type mismatch`).

message: a variant requires an enum type
internal: values.rs builds Variant only for MIR enum aggregates, whose destination has the enum's Rust type, and enum types always lower to Aggregate::Enum (types.rs enumeration, references.rs variant_type); other destinations fail in the importer with `an enum value requires an enum place`.

message: aggregate components must be owned values
aggregate constants require matching constant components
internal: literals.rs literal_at and variant_literal build each component as a constant of its layout field's own type, lowered like the aggregate's field (or zero of the slot type), never as a place.

values.rs builds Aggregate from MIR tuple, struct, closure and array aggregates with one operand per field (Repeat uses the array length), and their IR types keep every field, zero-sized ones as Unit (types.rs lower and with_spaces).

message: aggregate type {id} must reference earlier definitions
internal: TypeLowering interns every component type before the aggregate that contains it, so component IDs always precede their parent's.

Type lowering rejects never and buffer components ('aggregate components must be owned values'), zero-sized array elements and non-integer checked pairs, and checked_reference requires importer-built aggregates to match that lowering, all before validation.

message: an enum value names its variant
internal: values.rs sends MIR enum aggregates to Variant, so Aggregate is built only for tuples, structs, closures and arrays, whose IR types are never Aggregate::Enum.

message: an enum value requires an enum place
internal: MIR building constructs every enum aggregate into a local of the enum's own type (projected assignments go through a temporary, and constructors called as functions return into one), and enum types lower to enum aggregates or to Never or Unit, whose assignments are skipped.

message: array indices require a usize local
internal: MIR Index locals are usize and lower to Scalar::Usize; the only usize local with another IR type is a #[repr(usize)] discriminant read through the internal discriminant_value intrinsic, and indexing with it fails first at the bounds-check comparison (`invalid binary operation types`).

message: arrays of zero-sized values are unsupported

internal: Atomic operations come only from AtomicBuffer/AtomicThreadgroupBuffer methods, whose index parameter is typed u32.
The atomic methods type their value operands as the handle's element type T.

message: atomic operations require an i32/u32 atomic buffer
internal: Atomic operations come only from methods on atomic handles, and atomic buffers of other element types are rejected earlier: kernel parameters in collect.rs, other locals by validate's 'unsupported local type' check, which runs before statements are typed.

message: branch/assert condition must have bool type
internal: The importer emits Branch only for bool SwitchInt operands and its own bool comparisons, and MIR assert conditions are bool.

message: buffer access mode does not match its address space
internal: Type lowering gives threadgroup handles only ReadWrite or Atomic access.

message: buffer lengths and slices require an unmodified kernel buffer parameter
buffer load requires a read buffer
internal: BufferLoad is built only for load_unchecked on ReadBuffer, ReadWriteBuffer and (Dynamic)ThreadgroupBuffer (intrinsics/device.rs, signature checked in signatures.rs), whose receivers lower to Read or ReadWrite buffers (types.rs buffer).

buffer_parameter only returns a kernel parameter that a device buffer handle borrows, and the receivers of as_slice and get_mut are typed &ReadBuffer and &mut DisjointBuffer, whose parameters lower to ir::Type::Buffer.

message: buffer store requires a write buffer
internal: BufferStore is built only for store_unchecked on WriteBuffer, ReadWriteBuffer and (Dynamic)ThreadgroupBuffer with an element-typed value (signatures.rs), whose receivers lower to Write or ReadWrite buffers (types.rs buffer).

message: calling a kernel entrypoint is unsupported
cannot resolve a concrete device instance for {callee}

internal: monomorphize::validate resolves every reachable call with the same Instance::try_resolve query before import and aborts on Ok(None) with 'cannot resolve a concrete device instance', and Err is only returned after rustc has reported an error.
Cast comes from MIR IntToInt, IntToFloat, FloatToInt and FloatToFloat casts of primitive numbers, which lower to scalars, from the niche transmute's bool flag, and from the F16/F32 bridge calls.
Type::Checked is created only for (integer, bool) tuples (types.rs lower) and integer overflow operations, so Checked expressions built for those destinations always carry an integer scalar.

message: control flow requires excessive or cooperative block duplication
cooperative operation requires uniform participation; divergent control flow is unsupported
coroutines and other callable shims are not supported in Metal kernels

internal: Every crate a device build links (the kernel crate, core, compiler_builtins and metal_oxide_device) is compiled by this driver, whose config sets always_encode_mir, foreign items are rejected by the foreign-ABI check just before, and intrinsics and shims are not InstanceKind::Item, so every Item the collector reaches has MIR.

message: device instance depth exceeds the rustc recursion limit
device log arguments must be a tuple
internal: log::write's arguments implement the sealed Arguments trait, which only tuples of printable scalars implement, and such a tuple operand imports as a place, an aggregate constant or the unit constant, never a scalar constant.

message: device log formats must be string literals
device log formats support only `{}` placeholders

internal: Switch cases come from MIR SwitchInt values, which are distinct and fit the discriminant type the importer converts them to (enum tags are sized to the variant count).
The importer numbers each function's threadgroup allocations with a per-function counter.

message: dynamic array index bounds cannot be proved safe
internal: MIR indexes an array only through a fresh index temporary checked against the constant length by an enabled assert, which the analysis assumes before the access, and constant indices become field projections.
Type lowering maps zero-sized structs, tuples and closures to unit and rejects zero-length arrays, and enums always have a tag field.
Const evaluation validates enum constants, so a direct tag always equals one variant's discriminant.

message: enum constant of an uninhabited type
internal: variant_literal only runs for types that lower to an enum aggregate, and lower() maps uninhabited types, the only ones with Variants::Empty layouts, to Never.

message: enum {name} cannot cross the kernel ABI
internal: layout runs only on kernel parameters and their buffer elements, which collect::validate (types::parameter) and IR validation already require to be TypeTable::is_abi_value, and is_abi_value excludes enums.

message: f16 storage requires an explicit f32 conversion
internal: F16 is a device struct, so Rust `as` casts never take or produce it, and its private u16 is converted only by transmute (a Bitcast); the only F16 casts are the __metal_f16_from_f32 and __metal_f16_to_f32 bridges, F32 to F16 and back.
CleanupPostBorrowck, a required pass before runtime MIR, replaces every fake borrow with a Nop, so the optimized MIR the importer reads never contains one.

message: foreign ABI calls are not supported in Metal kernels

internal: calls.rs call passes one operand per MIR argument after spread, which untuples a rust-call tuple exactly when the callee body takes its arguments separately, and keys the callee on that same list, so the count equals the callee body's arg_count.
validate rejects block-less functions first with 'function requires return/parameter locals and an entry block' before building the control-flow graph, its only caller.

message: function requires return/parameter locals and an entry block
internal: The importer creates one IR local per MIR local, including the return place and arguments, and one block per MIR basic block.

message: indirect calls are not supported in Metal kernels

internal: monomorphize::validate visits the same bodies before import and reports every call whose callee type is not an FnDef as 'indirect calls are not supported in Metal kernels', aborting first.

message: integer division/remainder requires a proved nonzero divisor
integer operation requires a scalar operand
internal: IR validation, which Codegen::new runs before emission, types every Integer expression and already rejects a first argument that is not an integer scalar.

message: integer operation requires an integer scalar
internal: Integer ops come from core's integer intrinsics, which core calls only on integer types; integer_min and rotate_left are bounded to integers, and a direct ctpop::<f32> under #![feature(core_intrinsics)] is an invalid monomorphization (E0511) in a real build.
Only Dim3 struct expressions build aggregates of ir::Type::Dim3, and MIR gives them exactly the three operands x, y and z, also for functional record updates.
The importer rejects SIMD intrinsic calls of the wrong arity first ('invalid SIMD intrinsic arity'), and the device wrappers pass the right count.
signatures::valid rejects device SIMD declarations whose parameter count differs from SimdOp::arity before any call is imported, and type-checked calls pass exactly the declared parameters.

literals.rs builds an aggregate constant with exactly field_count components of its lowered type, and that type has fields: pointer types fail lowering (`unsupported device type`), empty aggregates fail the earlier type table check, and Unit and scalars become plain constants.

message: invalid aggregate field, index or dereference

internal: every Aggregate id the importer uses is interned in the module's type table (types.rs intern), so it is always in range.
The importer rejects atomic intrinsic calls of the wrong arity first ('invalid atomic intrinsic arity'), and the device methods pass the right count.
signatures::atomic_signature requires 2 + AtomicOp::arity() parameters for every atomic method, and type-checked calls pass exactly that many arguments.
Block targets are MIR basic block indices or blocks the importer appends after them.
MIR switches on a bool only with the value 0 and an otherwise target, and the filtered cases of such a switch always take one of the accepted shapes.
DisjointBuffer::get_mut, the only element query, takes exactly a receiver and a &ThreadIndex, as signatures::valid checks.
Reference inference types the result of get_mut as an Option of a device element pointer (call_result), and kernel buffers cannot have zero-sized elements whose references would lower to Unit.
Every buffer query is a method whose receiver is its first argument, so the argument list is never empty.
ir::Type::Checked is the lowering of two-field (integer, bool) tuples, so aggregates assigned to it always have two operands.
The ChunksExact local that an expanded next() advances is typed as core's ChunksExact record, whose field 0 is the slice of remaining chunks.
chunk_type types the destination of an expanded ChunksExact::next as an Option of the iterator's chunk slice, which next_chunk finds again.

MIR builds ConstantIndex projections on arrays from the array's own length (exact offsets with min_length equal to it, or from-end offsets within the pattern), and slice ConstantIndex projections fail earlier with 'slice patterns are unsupported'.
Each builtin's argument count is fixed by its core or device declaration, which signatures::valid checks for device intrinsics, so a type-checked call always passes the count the importer expects.

Only items of the crate named metal_oxide_device count as device operations (intrinsics/device.rs in_module), so kernel source cannot declare one, and every real metal_oxide_device declaration passes signatures::valid (a kernel calling every device operation compiles); only the malformed_device crates of support::invalid_device reach it.
the variant index comes from MIR, and IR enums keep one entry per Rust variant, uninhabited ones included (types.rs enumeration).
call ids come from the importer's function table, and import/mod.rs called keeps every callee of a kept function and renumbers the calls consistently.
Integer intrinsics are recognized only in core, whose declarations take exactly IntegerOp::arity() arguments.
calls.rs rejects a wrong arity as `invalid integer intrinsic arity` before it builds Integer.
places use MIR locals, each of which gets an IR local, or importer temporaries pushed onto the same list.
calls.rs rejects a wrong arity as `invalid math intrinsic arity` before it builds Math, and signatures.rs checks each bridge declaration against the op's arity.
Math intrinsics are core's f32 abs, min and max and device declarations whose arity signatures::valid checks, so calls always pass MathOp::arity() arguments.
Pointer types are created only by interning into the module's type table, so their IDs are always valid.
Expanded ranges are core's Range<T> of an integer T, which lowers to a record whose start and end fields have the scalar type of next's Option payload.
Range<T>::next returns Option<T> for an integer T, which lowers to the Option enum with one scalar payload.
The local that an expanded Range::next advances holds a Range<T> value, which lowers to a record aggregate.
Index::index and IndexMut::index_mut always take exactly a receiver and an index.
Range, RangeFrom and RangeTo always have the start or end field looked up, and a range operand imports as a place or an aggregate constant, never a scalar constant.

message: invalid static SIMD source control: maximum SIMD width is 64
irreducible control flow is not supported
internal: rustc builds MIR from structured control flow whose loops are entered only through their header, the driver forces mir-opt-level 0 for every crate so no jump threading runs, and the importer only removes edges or inserts single-entry blocks, so imported CFGs stay reducible.

message: kernel entrypoints must not have generic parameters
kernel entrypoints must use the Rust ABI
kernel name is not a supported MSL identifier

internal: collect.rs rejects non-unit kernel return types first with 'kernel entrypoints must return ()'.

message: kernels take at most 28 buffer and value parameters; the next slots carry the gate, failure and length words
length requires a slice or buffer
internal: Len comes from PtrMetadata of Rust slice pointers (a thin pointer's unit metadata is skipped as a zero-sized assignment), from buffer queries on device buffer kernel parameters, and from subslice and chunk temporaries; a subslice of a zero-sized array reference fails reference inference first (`unsupported reference type`).

message: log arguments must be integers, f32 or F16
internal: log::write requires the sealed Arguments trait, implemented only for tuples of Value types (u8, u16, u32, u64, usize, i8, i16, i32, f32, F16), which all lower to non-bool scalars.
IR validation rejects any log argument that is not a non-bool scalar ("log arguments must be integers, f32 or F16") before codegen runs.

message: never parameters, unit kernel parameters and diverging functions are unsupported
internal: collect::validate and IR validation reject kernel parameters that are not ABI values and kernels that do not return unit, IR validation rejects every call statement that writes or passes a never-typed local (place_info: "never-typed values cannot be read"), and import drops functions that no statement calls.

message: pointer casts keep the pointee type and address space
internal: conversions.rs pointer_cast builds PointerCast only after the same same_values, address space and slice checks, and otherwise reports `pointer casts must keep the pointee type and address space` itself.
conversions.rs pointer_cast builds PointerCast only when both the operand type and the destination type are interned pointers.

References to zero-sized values lower to unit, and references to buffers or uninhabited values fail lowering ('aggregate components must be owned values', 'unsupported reference type') before validation.

message: range iteration requires an integer element
internal: Only Range<T> with an integral T is expanded, and every integer type that lowers becomes an integer scalar.
MIR index operands are temporaries assigned before their bounds check, and the importer assigns the index locals it creates before using them.
The borrow checker guarantees MIR reads only initialized locals, and the locals whose assignments the importer skips (buffer handles, messages, unused locals) are typed unit, which the check exempts.
monomorphize::validate reports recursive instances first ('recursion is not supported in Metal kernels') and the driver aborts before import.

message: recursion is not supported in Metal kernels

internal: values.rs and buffers.rs always build Ref with an Operand::Place.

message: signed division/remainder requires a proved MIN/-1 exclusion

internal: SinCos is built only for the __metal_sin_cos_f32 bridge, whose declaration signatures.rs checks to return (f32, f32), so its call destination lowers to and interns that tuple.

message: slice elements are not one value
internal: MIR never copies or moves an unsized [T] place, element places reach only Ref (which accepts them) or index projections, and destinations go through typed_place, which rejects them itself (`a slice is not one value`).

message: slice index is not below a checked slice length
slices are indexed by usize ranges
slices require an array or buffer

internal: Subslices come only from the importer's range-index expansion, which first asserts start <= end <= len on the same operands, and from the ChunksExact expansion guarded by size <= len.

Subslice is built by the subslice expansion on a slice receiver or an array's slice temporary and by the chunk iterator on its slice field; a zero-sized array receiver fails reference inference of the call result first (`unsupported reference type`).

message: switch case type must match discriminant
internal: The importer converts every case value to the discriminant's own scalar type.

message: switch discriminant must be an integer
internal: The importer lowers bool switches to Branch and rejects other non-integer discriminants itself ('unsupported switch discriminant type').

message: threadgroup allocations inside loops are unsupported
threadgroup allocations must be in kernel entrypoints
unchecked conversion requires an integer target
internal: UncheckedCast is built for f32::to_int_unchecked::<Int>, whose sealed FloatToInt<Int> bound admits only integer types.

message: unchecked float conversion requires a scalar
internal: f32::to_int_unchecked targets a type implementing the sealed FloatToInt, a primitive integer, which lowers to a scalar or fails first as an unsupported device type.
The borrow checker guarantees MIR initializes the return place on every returning path, and return places the importer types unit (messages, handles) are exempt.

message: uninitialized storage has no value expression
internal: structured.rs skips Uninit statements before it calls expressions::expression, the only caller of that function.

message: uninitialized storage must be an array
internal: Uninit takes the lowering of [T; N], which is an array or an importer error, except for an uninhabited T, where the call's destination is never-typed and validation reports `never-typed values cannot be read` first.

message: unsized coercions require an array reference

internal: MIR building constructs non-enum aggregates into locals of their own type, which lower to records, tuples, arrays, Checked, Dim3 or Unit, while restricted wrappers take the is_wrapping path and F16 and buffer handles are only built inside the device crate by transmute or by intrinsics whose bodies are not imported.

The other AssertKinds come from coroutine resumption, whose instances never reach import, and from the null, alignment and enum UB-check passes, which the driver disables with ub_checks = false; forced on with -Zmir-enable-passes they still emit pointer-to-integer transmutes or u128 temporaries that are rejected before their assertions.

The only BinOp the importer lacks is Cmp, whose result type core::cmp::Ordering has explicit discriminants, so the local receiving it first fails lowering with 'explicit enum discriminants are unsupported'.
MIR's UnOp has only Not, Neg and PtrMetadata, and an earlier match arm handles PtrMetadata.

The importer emits Cast only for MIR int/float casts (Rust rejects `as bool` and `bool as f32`), for niche tags from a bool flag to a U8/U16/U32 tag, and for F16/F32 conversions, so no cast targets bool or turns bool into f32.
Numeric casts target primitive numbers, which lower to scalars or make the destination local fail lowering first as an unsupported device type.
Only Rust enum ADTs lower to enum aggregates, so variant_literal always sees an ADT type.
collect.rs validates kernel parameters with the same type lowering first, reporting 'unsupported kernel parameter type: {ty}', and the driver aborts before import.
MIR building emits Overflow assertions only for Add, Sub, Mul, Shl, Shr, Div and Rem.
Bitcast comes from transmutes that values.rs already checks for equal widths and no bool, and from f32::to_bits and from_bits (F32 to U32 and back).
SwitchInt operands are bools, integers or chars; char fails lowering first, integer locals lower to integer scalars, and discriminant locals take their enum's integer tag.
emit.rs rejects every reachable Unreachable terminator before structured::body runs, and path visits only reachable blocks, handles Panic before its match, and matches every other terminator.

message: unsupported value in kernel ABI layout
internal: layout runs only on kernel parameters and their buffer elements, which collect::validate and IR validation already restrict to scalars and non-enum aggregates of ABI values.

IR variants drop only the fields of variants with an uninhabited field, and a value for such a variant comes from a Use temporary or a call argument, which monomorphize::body turns into unreachable, or from a call result whose never-typed destination fails first with `never-typed values cannot be read`.

After rustc's Derefer pass every MIR place dereferences only its base local, whose IR pointer keeps its Rust mutability, and Rust permits no writes through shared pointers (UnsafeCell pointer casts fail in the importer).
The borrow checker guarantees a pointer is initialized before a write through it, and the importer rejects dereferencing the handle locals it leaves unassigned.
bool, usize and isize are not ABI values, so collect::validate and IR validation reject kernel parameters and buffer elements that hold them before codegen lays out the interface.
